title: Sec. 37.15 Reporting Obligations; Licensing
statement: Owners must report unit data under penalty of perjury; condominiums and units in buildings with fewer than 10 units report from March 1, 2023 and annually by March 1; substantially compliant owners receive a license to impose rent increases; otherwise the license is suspended and the tenant is not obligated to pay the increased rent for months during the suspension. Added by Ord. 265-20.

title: Annual rent increase for multiple years
statement: Increase for two or more years by adding the allowable percentages; increases cannot be compounded; no petition required for these increases; no rounding up; 30-day notice (35 if mailed); base rent only.

title: Rent Board Portal
statement: Official portal to create an owner account, report into the Housing Inventory and check Rent Increase License status by address or APN.

title: The Rent Board Fee
statement: Separate from the Rent Increase License: every residential dwelling unit owner must pay a per-unit Rent Board Fee unless exempt. 2026-2027: $59.00 per dwelling unit, $29.50 per guest unit. Due March 1 each year; 5% monthly late penalty to a 15% maximum; unpaid balances referred to the Bureau of Delinquent Revenue after June 1. If the fee is paid in full, 50% ($29.50 per dwelling unit) may be recovered from tenants in occupancy as of November 1 of the tax year; penalties may not be recovered. 'Requesting a Rent Board Fee exemption does not satisfy Rent Board Housing Inventory reporting requirements.' Re-verified 2026-11-07.

title: CIV 1942.5 (retaliation)
statement: If the lessee is not in default and has exercised repair/tenantability rights or complained to an agency, the lessor may not increase the rent (or decrease services) within 180 days of the triggering act; separate bar on retaliating for tenant organizing or exercising lawful rights; remedy is actual damages plus punitive damages of $100-$2,000 per retaliatory act for fraud/oppression/malice, and the court awards attorney's fees to the prevailing party if requested. Operative October 1, 2021. Re-verified 2026-11-07.

title: CIV 1947.12 (AB 1482) - two-unit exemption text
statement: The state rent cap does not apply to a property with two separate dwelling units in a single structure where the owner occupied one unit as the principal residence at the beginning of the tenancy and continues in occupancy, and neither unit is an ADU or JADU. Exemption for separately alienable property requires the owner notice and that the owner is not a REIT, corporation, or an LLC with at least one corporate member. Verified from the statute text 2026-11-07.

title: Partial Exemption for Newly Constructed Rental Units
statement: Units whose first Certificate of Occupancy issued after June 13, 1979 are exempt from the rent increase limitations only; they keep just-cause eviction protection and the annual Rent Board fee is collected for them. The exemption needs both a post-June-13-1979 first Certificate of Occupancy and no residential use before it. Re-verified 2026-11-07.

title: Partial Exemption for Certain Single-Family Homes and Condominiums Under Costa-Hawkins
statement: As of January 1, 1999, single-family homes and condominiums are generally exempt from the rent increase limitations (but not just cause) only if the tenancy commenced on or after January 1, 1996; a tenancy that commenced before that date stays fully covered. A single-family dwelling with a LEGAL in-law unit constitutes a two-unit building and is not exempt. A single-family dwelling with an ILLEGAL in-law unit also constitutes a two-unit building and is not exempt UNLESS both units are rented together as a single tenancy. A single-family dwelling is not exempt if another residential structure is on the same lot. Exempt units still owe the annual Rent Board fee. Wording corrected 2026-11-08 after line-by-line comparison with the page (see flag F36).

title: Evictions in San Francisco
statement: Eviction requires just cause under the Rent Ordinance; the Rent Ordinance generally allows tenants to replace departing roommates and to increase the number of occupants even when a written lease prohibits it; free legal help through the Eviction Defense Collaborative (415-659-9184) on receipt of an unlawful detainer; the 17 just-cause reasons are listed separately. Re-verified 2026-11-07.

title: Recover part of your Rent Board fee from the tenant
statement: A landlord who has paid the Rent Board fee in full may collect 50% (excluding late penalties) from the tenant(s) residing in the unit, and only if the tenant resided there on or before November 1 of the year before the fee became due. Recovery is by deducting the amount from the annual security-deposit interest payment, or by billing directly only where there is no or insufficient deposit held or the landlord already pays interest annually. The bill must state the fee amount for each year, any deposit interest owed, that the purpose is to fund the Rent Board, and that the fee is due within 30 days. Unrecovered fees may be banked. A tenant's failure to pay is not a just cause for eviction; collection is through Small Claims Court. Re-verified 2026-11-08.

title: Chapter 37A Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Fee (official PDF)
statement: Sec. 37A.1 makes the chapter apply to all residential units, including units exempt from the Chapter 37 rent-increase limits under Costa-Hawkins or Sec. 37.3(d). Sec. 37A.4: fees are due March 1, with 5% added if unpaid by March 1, a further 5% if unpaid by April 1, and a further 5% if unpaid by May 1; referrals to the Bureau of Delinquent Revenue after June 1. Sec. 37A.6: recovery limited to 50% of the annual fee, exclusive of penalties, from tenants in occupancy on November 1, by deposit-interest deduction or a compliant direct bill, may be banked for fees due after July 25, 1999, and the owner remains liable for the full fee whether or not recovery is sought. Re-verified 2026-11-08.

Earlier rows are $50.00 (7/19-6/21), $45.00, $40.00, $37.00, $36.00, $29.00, $26.00, $22.00, $20.00, $27.00, $19.00 and $16.00. Title says 25-26 and has no 2026-2027 row (see flag F40). Re-verified 2026-11-08.

title: Notification of Rent Board Fee and Housing Inventory Requirements (2027 Informational Notice)
statement: 2027 informational notice: no payment is required at this time; the assessment is the basis for the Annual Fee Notice mailed in January 2027; vacant units are subject to the fee and do not qualify for an exemption; an exemption request must be submitted every year by Monday, December 14, 2026; requesting a fee exemption does not satisfy Housing Inventory reporting; Housing Inventory reporting is due March 1, 2027 and annually; landlords will not receive a rent increase license until reporting is complete; occupants of unreported units may receive a noncompliance notice; some increases given without a license will be null and void. Re-verified 2026-11-08.

title: Information for Lessors of Residential Real Estate
statement: A person receiving rental income from one residential structure consisting of fewer than four units (or one residential condominium) is not, by reason of that fact alone, required to obtain a business registration certificate; other business activity or payroll may require one. For the Gross Receipts Tax and Business Registration Fee a lessor is treated as a separate person for each individual building, and the Tax Collector decides what constitutes a separate building and the number of units. A lessor must file a return unless leasing fewer than 4 units in any individual building, and is exempt from the Gross Receipts Tax if leasing fewer than 4 units in any individual building. Re-verified 2026-11-08.

title: Security Deposits (interest rate and AB 12 deposit cap)
statement: The security-deposit interest rate for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 4.2%; interest is owed annually on the tenant's annual due date for deposits held over one year and may not be compounded. AB 12 caps a dwelling-unit deposit at one month's rent for deposits collected on or after July 1, 2024, with an exception allowing two months' rent where the owner is a natural person (or an LLC whose members are all natural persons) and owns no more than 2 residential rental properties totalling no more than 4 dwelling units offered for rent. Re-verified 2026-11-08.

title: File No. 261020 - Administrative Code - Cap On Rent Increases for Rent-Controlled Units
statement: Ordinance amending the Administrative Code so that banked rent increases and capital improvement rent increases for rent-controlled units may not raise a tenant's rent by more than a total of 10% per year, for the next three years. Introduced 9/15/2026; sponsors Sauter, Chan, Mahmood; STATUS AT FETCH: 'Pending Committee Action', in control of the Land Use and Transportation Committee, no final action and no enactment date, version 1, four history records (9/15/2026 assigned under 30-day rule; 9/18/2026 and 9/30/2026 referred to department; 10/7/2026 Youth Commission response received). NOT ENACTED - it is not law and creates no current limit. Direct fetch_page 2026-11-10.

title: Notice: Proposed Changes to Rent Increase Limitations (posted November 9, 2026 on S01 and S02)
statement: Official Rent Board notice present on both the 'Learn about rent increases in San Francisco' page (S01) and the 'Current Rates' page (S02), posted November 9, 2026: the Board of Supervisors is considering legislation (File No. 261020) that would temporarily limit the combined amount of banked rent increases and capital improvement rent increases that may be imposed on rent-controlled units to 10% per year; if enacted as currently proposed it would apply to banked rent increases noticed on or after September 15, 2026 and capital improvement rent increases based on petitions filed with the Rent Board on or after September 15, 2026; 'This legislation has not been enacted and is subject to change.' Direct fetch_page of both pages 2026-11-10.
